events.continuity_hook: The outbound, hotel, panel schedule, and bag-storage arrangement remain unchanged; only the reissued return ticket and seat assignment need final verification.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm that the later nonstop is fully ticketed without an additional fare, verify the updated arrival time, and select an available seat on the replacement flight.
events.scenario_brief: The airline has reissued Danielle’s Thursday return on the later Denver-to-Dallas nonstop after the schedule change. The new confirmation shows the correct departure, but the ticket receipt needs to be checked for an added collection and her previously assigned seat no longer appears.

events.continuity_hook: The two event times and venue addresses are known, but flights, hotel, and airport transfers have not been selected.
events.interaction_goal: Develop complete one-night trip options, compare nonstop schedules and hotel locations, estimate ground transportation, and identify combinations that fit the allowance with workable arrival and departure margins.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle needs to attend a Tuesday afternoon funder roundtable and a Wednesday morning youth-arts workshop in Minneapolis. She can depart Dallas Tuesday morning and return after the workshop, needs one hotel night with practical access to both venues, and has a fixed organizational allowance covering airfare, lodging, and airport transportation.

events.continuity_hook: The remaining hotel candidates are available for either itinerary, so the flight schedule must be settled before comparing their payment deadlines.
events.interaction_goal: Compare total fares, ticket terms, airport-transfer times, and realistic margins around both events, then choose the outbound and return pairing.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle has narrowed the Minneapolis flights to an earlier Tuesday nonstop that provides a comfortable roundtable margin and a cheaper departure arriving shortly before the event. Two Wednesday returns remain: an afternoon flight requiring a prompt departure after the workshop and an evening flight that adds several hours but has a lower fare.

events.continuity_hook: Flights are settled, and the one-night hotel is the last unbooked part of the Minneapolis trip.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate comparable hotel totals, confirm payment and cancellation dates, assess travel time to the workshop and airport, verify bag storage, and book the option that keeps the trip within the allowance.
events.scenario_brief: With the earlier Tuesday outbound and afternoon Wednesday return selected, Danielle is choosing between a hotel beside the roundtable venue and a lower-priced property near a direct transit route to the workshop. The closer hotel has a mandatory facility fee, while the second requires advance payment and lists breakfast separately; both indicate post-checkout bag storage.

events.continuity_hook: The school-break dates and four-night duration are fixed, but transportation in both directions, lodging area, room layout, and the full family cost remain open.
events.interaction_goal: Compare complete flight and train combinations, account for station or airport transfers and baggage terms, evaluate representative rooms for three-person occupancy, and establish which trip structures fit the family’s budget.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle, her spouse, and their daughter are planning a four-night fall-break trip to New Orleans. They are comparing nonstop flights with an overnight train in one direction, want one room that clearly accommodates three guests, and need to decide whether staying in the Warehouse District or near City Park works better for their planned museum, music, and garden visits.

events.continuity_hook: Two hotels in different neighborhoods remain under consideration, but their arrival-night logistics and final totals depend on the flight pair selected.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the four flight pairings by schedule, ticket restrictions, baggage cost, and total family fare, then select an itinerary that preserves useful time in New Orleans without exceeding the transportation budget.
events.scenario_brief: The family has ruled out the overnight train after comparing travel time and sleeping arrangements. Danielle is now weighing two outbound nonstops and two return flights: the lowest fares use restrictive tickets and leave limited time on the first and last days, while the better-timed options cost more and differ in included carry-on and checked-bag allowances for three travelers.
